context: Machine Learning / Reinforcement Learning Fundamentals. No authored doc.md exists for this course; each lesson is grounded in its live topic list and its existing quiz bank (source.md).

topics: States, Actions, and the Agent-Environment Loop
Transition Probabilities and the Markov Property
Reward Functions and Return (Cumulative Discounted Reward)
Episodic vs. Continuing Tasks
Discount Factor Gamma: Short-Sighted vs. Far-Sighted Agents
Formalizing a Real Problem as an MDP
laterLessonsCover: Value Functions and Bellman Equations: Policies as State-to-Action Mappings, State-Value Function V(s) and Action-Value Function Q(s,a), Bellman Expectation Equation for V and Q, Hand-Computing a One-Step Bellman Update on a Small Gridworld, Bellman Optimality Equation and Optimal Policies

Dynamic Programming: Policy and Value Iteration: Iterative Policy Evaluation, Policy Improvement and the Policy Iteration Loop, Value Iteration as Truncated Policy Iteration, Convergence and the Role of Gamma in DP, Why Model-Based DP Breaks Down in Practice (Curse of Dimensionality)

Monte Carlo vs. Temporal-Difference Learning: Monte Carlo Returns from Complete Episodes, First-Visit vs. Every-Visit MC Prediction, TD(0): Bootstrapping from the Next State's Estimate, TD Error as a Learning Signal, MC vs. TD: Bias, Variance, and Episodic Requirements

Tabular Q-Learning and SARSA: On-Policy vs. Off-Policy Learning, Q-Learning: Off-Policy TD Control via the Max Operator, SARSA: On-Policy TD Control Update, Hyperparameters: Learning Rate Alpha, Gamma, Epsilon, Implementing Tabular Q-Learning in Python (NumPy), Diagnosing Convergence on a Gridworld Environment
Exploration vs. Exploitation: The Exploration-Exploitation Trade-off, Greedy and Epsilon-Greedy Action Selection, Epsilon Decay Schedules, Optimistic Initialization and Softmax/Boltzmann Exploration

From Tables to Policy Gradients: Why Tabular Methods Fail in Large/Continuous State Spaces, Value Function Approximation with Neural Networks (DQN Intuition), Parameterized Policies and the Policy Gradient Objective, Score Function / Log-Derivative Trick Intuition, REINFORCE: Monte Carlo Policy Gradient, Advantage Functions and Actor-Critic at a Glance

RLHF and Reward Models for LLM Alignment: LLM Fine-Tuning Framed as an MDP (Tokens as Actions), Learning a Reward Model from Human Preference Comparisons, Bradley-Terry Preference Modeling for Reward Training, KL Penalty: Staying Close to the Reference Policy, PPO-Style Policy Optimization Against the Reward Model, Reward Hacking and Limits of Learned Reward Models
